title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Bhutan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Bhutan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Bhutan: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: Following a death in Bhutan, civil registration is managed through the Department of Civil Registration and Census (DCRC) under the Bhutan Civil Registration System, while succession and land transfers follow the Inheritance Act of Bhutan and Royal Court of Justice procedures [1] [2] [3]. We outline the five core administrative steps below, including NPPF surviving-family claims and Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation rules since Bhutan is not an Apostille Convention party [4] [7] [8].

steps.title: Register the death with DCRC or local census offices
steps.html:
• Choose your registration office: Under the Department of Civil Registration and Census (DCRC) Revised Guidelines, death registration may be filed at the current place of residence or permanent census address via any Community Service Centre (CSC), Thromde Civil Registration and Census Office (TCRCO), Drungkhag/Dzongkhag Civil Registration and Census Office (DrCRCO / DzCRCO), or DCRC HQ [1] [2].
  • Submit required documents: Bring completed application form BCRS-DR-01, the original Citizenship Identity (CID) or Special Resident (SR) card of the deceased, and a Notification of Death (for deaths inside a health facility) [1] [2]. For deaths outside a health facility, a Guarantor (Bhutanese citizen aged 18 to 65 from another household) and a Witness (Bhutanese citizen aged 18+ from another household) must attend in person with Statement of Death form BCRS-DR-SD-01 [1] [2].
  • Register early rather than waiting for the Annual Census: Although census books also update at the Annual Census, registering immediately is vital to obtain an official Death Certificate for Rural Life Insurance (RLI), NPPF benefits, bank clearances, and inheritance petitions [2].

steps.title: Handle funeral customs and foreign document attestation
steps.html:
• Coordinate local funeral and health clearances: Obtain hospital release or local medical notification before traditional cremation or burial rites; if an unnatural or unexpected death occurred, police and hospital forensic clearance comes first [2].
  • Document attestation instead of Hague Apostille: Per the HCCH status table, Bhutan is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [8]. Official documents such as Death Certificates, Household Information records, or Inheritance clearances required outside Bhutan must first be notarized by the Public Notary Office and then submitted to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade (Department of Protocol and Consular Affairs) [7].
  • Attestation schedule and fees: Consular Affairs receives attestation applications (with declaration form and original document; laminated originals are rejected) on Mondays and Thursdays (9:00 AM to 1:00 PM) and returns attested papers on Tuesdays and Fridays (10:00 AM to 1:00 PM) for Nu. 300 per applicant, followed by any receiving embassy legalization [7].

steps.title: Claim NPPF survivor pensions, provident fund, and insurance
steps.html:
• Notify the National Pension and Provident Fund (NPPF): For deceased civil servants, armed forces personnel, or corporate members, notify the National Pension and Provident Fund (NPPF) (toll-free 1039 or WhatsApp 17170884) regarding Provident Fund (Tier 2) lump-sum balances and monthly Surviving Family Benefits [9] [10].
  • Check beneficiary eligibility rules: Under NPPF rules, up to three surviving children under age 18, an eligible surviving spouse (immediately for armed forces personnel, or from age 50 for civil service members), or surviving parents (where no spouse or child survives) qualify for monthly pension benefits; beneficiaries must submit certified non-remarriage certificates annually on or before 30 April [9].
  • Claim Rural Life Insurance and employer gratuity: Submit the DCRC Death Certificate to Gewog/Thromde offices for Rural Life Insurance (RLI) and to employers or RICBL for group insurance and gratuity settlements [2] [9].

steps.title: Settle inheritance through the Courts and land registries
steps.html:
• Probate wills or apply joint-family intestacy: Under Chapter VII (Sections Ga 7-1 to Ga 7-14) of the Inheritance Act of Bhutan 1980, valid written wills signed before witnesses and presented to a Court of Law (or oral declarations before two witnesses reduced to writing within 30 days) govern distribution; absent a valid will, Chapter VIII joint-family inheritance rules apply through the Royal Court of Justice (Judiciary of Bhutan) [3] [6].
  • Note citizenship rules on immovable property: Under Section Ga 6-23 of the Inheritance Act, non-Bhutanese spouses or children who have not acquired Bhutanese citizenship may inherit movable property only and cannot inherit immovable land or buildings [3].
  • Update land titles via eSakor: Once the court settles inheritance rights, process thram and land title transfers through the National Land Commission Secretariat (NLCS eSakor portal) and local Dzongkhag Land Offices [11].

steps.title: Close bank accounts and confirm representation from abroad
steps.html:
• Use a Jabmi or Power of Attorney if absent: Under Section 148 of the Civil and Criminal Procedure Code of Bhutan 2001 and the Jabmi Act, family members or parties residing away from the district may appoint a family representative, holder of a Power of Attorney, or licensed Jabmi (advocate) before the Court [4] [5].
  • Clear financial institutions and utilities: Provide certified copies of the DCRC Death Certificate and court inheritance orders to Bank of Bhutan or other financial institutions to release funds and close loans [2] [3].

closingQuestion: Which Dzongkhag or Thromde was the deceased registered in, and do family members need Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation for overseas use?

contacts.name: Department of Civil Registration and Census (DCRC)
contacts.note: Administers the Bhutan Civil Registration System (BCRS-DR-01 death registration and official Death Certificates) via DzCRCO, TCRCO, DrCRCO, and CSC offices.

contacts.name: National Pension and Provident Fund (NPPF)
contacts.note: Toll-free helpline 1039 (WhatsApp 17170884) handles member Provident Fund death disbursements and Surviving Family Benefits.

contacts.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade
contacts.note: Department of Protocol and Consular Affairs attests notarized Death Certificates and civil records (Nu. 300 fee) since Bhutan is not an Apostille party.

contacts.name: Royal Court of Justice (Judiciary of Bhutan)
contacts.note: Dzongkhag and Drungkhag Courts adjudicate wills, inheritance petitions under the Inheritance Act 1980, and formal legal clearances.
